backing.collateral_ratio_basis: Issuer-attested collateralization, published unchanged. NETTED ON BOTH SIDES: (reserves - POL - inventory) / (supply - POL - inventory), the basis apyx switched to on 2026-06-08. POL is protocol-owned liquidity and Inventory is a net-zero bucket, so both are removed from backing and from supply rather than counted as either. ⚠️ NOT comparable to a gross collateral ratio: the generic axis cutoffs assume gross, so a netted figure sits lower for the same underlying coverage. We verify the identity independently — residual tolerance 0.01pp — rather than trusting the attested number on its own; see asset_specific.backing_attestation.attested_basis_residual_pp. ⚠️ Netting makes this asset look WORSE, not better: gross is 99.20% against the netted 98.86%, -0.34pp. Do not read a netted basis as issuer-flattering.
backing.axis_rating_basis: Rated on the generic band deliberately — no anchor exists in this analyzer, and the apparent agreement between the axis (2/5) and the published backing score (2.0/10) is COINCIDENTAL. The axis rates coverage; the score rates basket composition (~74% STRC) and dislocation, which a collateral ratio cannot express. Expect them to diverge when STRC moves without the CR moving — that is the design, not a defect.
backing.surplus_deficit_basis: GROSS reserves minus GROSS supply — not netted, unlike collateral_ratio. ⚠️ B/(B - surplus_deficit) therefore recovers 99.22%, not the published 98.88%; the two fields are not coherent on one denominator. Use collateral_ratio for coverage and this only for the absolute gross gap.
